audit_title: VOXSHIELD Phase 2A.1 — Telephony / Channel Robustness Environment Audit

frozen_model.training_provenance: VCC2020 + VCC2018 (97 attack systems, 0 A07-A19 exposure, 0 speaker overlap)
frozen_model.status: STRICTLY FROZEN (No retraining, no threshold modification)

environment.hardware: Intel Core i5-1235U CPU (10 cores / 12 threads), 15.7 GB RAM

existing_pipeline_behavior.waveform_normalization: Integer range detection (>1.0 divides by 32768.0), zero-centering DC offset removal, pre-emphasis filter (alpha=0.97)
existing_pipeline_behavior.cropping_and_padding: Deterministic prefix crop if >= 48,000 samples; deterministic zero-padding at end if < 48,000 samples
feature_channels: Channel 0: Log-Mel Spectrogram (60 bins, 80 Hz - 8000 Hz, standardized)
Channel 1: LFCC Spectrogram (60 linear filterbank bins, DCT-II, standardized)
existing_pipeline_behavior.compatibility_with_telephony: The feature extractor strictly expects 16,000 Hz 1D tensors. Telephony audio sampled at 8 kHz (or compressed via G.711/AMR) MUST undergo round-trip resampling (16 kHz -> 8 kHz -> 16 kHz) prior to feature extraction so the time dimension remains exactly 301 frames and frequency bins remain aligned.

8khz_resampling.mechanism: torchaudio.transforms.Resample(16000, 8000) followed by Resample(8000, 16000), or scipy.signal.resample_poly

telephone_bandpass.mechanism: scipy.signal.butter 4th order bandpass (300 Hz - 3400 Hz) via sosfilt

additive_noise.mechanism: numpy.random.normal scaled to target SNR (e.g., 15 dB or 20 dB)

amplitude_variation.mechanism: Linear scaling factor (e.g. 0.5x, 1.5x) or random dB gain

synthetic_reverberation.mechanism: scipy.signal.fftconvolve with synthetic exponentially decaying noise impulse response

real_measured_rirs.reason: Realistic acoustic impulse responses require downloading an external RIR dataset (e.g., BUT Reverb DB or Aachen Impulse Response Database).

real_world_environmental_noise.reason: Realistic non-stationary ambient noise (e.g. urban, cafe, office, traffic) requires downloading a noise library (e.g., MUSAN or DEMAND).

voip_packet_loss_simulation.reason: Requires dedicated network emulation software (NetEm) or a specialized Gilbert-Elliott packet loss simulator script.

recommended_evaluation_matrix.expected_effect: Reference baseline performance established in Phase 1C.5 (ROC-AUC 0.9026, F1 0.6860, EER 18.33%).
recommended_evaluation_matrix.why_it_matters: Provides the untouched anchor point to measure relative degradation under channel distortion.

recommended_evaluation_matrix.expected_effect: Eliminates all acoustic content above 4,000 Hz Nyquist frequency, stripping high-frequency vocoder harmonics.
recommended_evaluation_matrix.why_it_matters: Isolates the pure effect of standard telephony bandwidth downsampling without non-linear companding.

recommended_evaluation_matrix.transformation: G.711 mu-law (8 kHz, 8-bit logarithmic companding, 64 kbps)
recommended_evaluation_matrix.expected_effect: Quantization distortion, dynamic range compression, and high-frequency cutoff.
recommended_evaluation_matrix.why_it_matters: Standard landline and VoIP telephony protocol in North America and Japan; primary carrier format for IVR fraud.

recommended_evaluation_matrix.transformation: G.711 A-law (8 kHz, 8-bit logarithmic companding, 64 kbps)
recommended_evaluation_matrix.expected_effect: Quantization distortion with piecewise-linear A-law curve, distinct from mu-law.
recommended_evaluation_matrix.why_it_matters: Mandatory standard for Indian telecom carriers, European cellular networks, and international gateways.

recommended_evaluation_matrix.transformation: ITU-T G.151 telephone bandpass filter (300 Hz - 3400 Hz)
recommended_evaluation_matrix.expected_effect: Attenuates low-frequency pitch harmonics (<300 Hz) and high-frequency spectral cues (>3400 Hz).
recommended_evaluation_matrix.why_it_matters: Simulates acoustic characteristics of physical landline telephone earpieces and microphones.

recommended_evaluation_matrix.transformation: Additive Gaussian noise at 15 dB SNR
recommended_evaluation_matrix.expected_effect: Masks subtle spectral energy differentials in quiet phonemes and unvoiced fricatives.
recommended_evaluation_matrix.why_it_matters: Simulates typical ambient noise levels during a mobile phone voice call.

evaluation_dataset.speaker_separation: Strict 0 speaker overlap with source-disjoint training (20 speakers) and validation (6 speakers)
evaluation_dataset.attack_separation: Strict 0 attack-system overlap with source-disjoint training (VCC2020+VCC2018, 97 systems)

methodology_constraints: The source-disjoint MiniAcousticCNN checkpoint (best_source_disjoint_mini_acoustic_cnn.pt) must remain frozen.
Original evaluation audio files must remain untouched; transformed copies or in-memory arrays will be evaluated.
Original ground-truth labels (0 for bonafide, 1 for spoof) must be preserved without alteration.
Test labels from the transformed audio must never be used to tune thresholds or select models.
Primary evaluation for every channel condition must use the frozen default threshold of 0.50.
Each condition must be evaluated and reported independently alongside the clean baseline.
risks_and_limitations: Nyquist bandlimiting at 8 kHz strips all spectral content between 4,000 Hz and 8,000 Hz, leaving Channel 0 (Log-Mel) and Channel 1 (LFCC) zeroed out in upper frequency bins.
Without telephony-augmented re-training, significant degradation in raw sensitivity (Recall) is expected when applying clean-trained models to 8 kHz G.711 channels.
Synthetic Gaussian noise provides a controlled benchmark but does not model realistic non-stationary street/traffic noise.
